# Reviewer/323 — round 1

Head: `134b0109a468024892eccf161392e1272d3bfa58`.

**Verdict: PASS WITH NOTES.** No new correctness blocker. Instance grouping and assign warning mutations are independently killed; all sixteen restored controls are green.

The duplicate identity is correct for this advice: `(role, instance, distinct seat)`, within the already-selected project. The bare role's empty instance is its own holding, not a wildcard for duplicate detection. A bare holder beside a named-instance holder is not a duplicate; two distinct live seats on the same bare or named holding are. Repeated rows for one seat alone do not create an action. Dead and closed holdings are filtered before grouping; `holders: many` receives no one-holder advice.

Grouping preserves the input's oldest-first order, so each duplicate group keeps the existing open-work/newest-seat selection. The release filter compares seat identity rather than row pointer: older repeated rows belonging to the kept seat cannot produce a release of that seat. Commands preserve the holding's instance and `--project`, pass through the existing shell quoting and printable-key guards, and do not mutate anything automatically.

Consumer closure was checked with hidden-source-aware searches: directory JSON computes the groups; the CLI renders that same `view["actions"]`; the `unanswered_by_holder` read is gated by the shared grouping helper; assign warning compares same instance and excludes the same seat. No second old duplicate-advice computation was found. The remaining `live.len() > 1` in the FYI binding path concerns a pane's seat identity, not role holdings.

`E-RS-ROLE-HOLDERS` remains separate and unchanged in `delivery/role_send.rs`. A bare role send can still be ambiguous across holdings even where no holding is duplicated; that is a routing refusal, not justification for releasing unrelated per-PR holdings. This PR does not weaken the multi-holder routing refusal or convert a warning into an admission refusal.

**N323-1 (existing, non-blocking qualification):** assign's warning checks an open holding row, not current seat liveness. An old open row on a dead seat may still warn when assigning another seat to the same instance; this was true before the PR. The operating picture correctly excludes the dead seat from duplicate-release advice. Do not broaden this fix into a new lifecycle/admission policy merely to align that existing warning's wording.

The corrected duplicate classification is a **POLICY** fix for advice: changing the holding key changes which releases are recommended. It is not a retention rule or a newly executed destructive action. The existing open-work and printable-key checks are **BRAKES** on producing executable release advice. No live holding was assigned or released in this review.

Cost: no new timer, poll, process launch, or steady-state fleet tick. The grouping is in-process over already-loaded rows, with allocation and worst-case `O(H * I)` comparisons for H live rows and I instances, once in the action renderer and once in the read gate. Thus “none” means no external/recurring work, not literally zero CPU. The open-work store read now runs only for a real duplicate group.

## Validation

`just pr-freeze 323`: initially exit 0, FINAL/CLEAN at the requested head, latest five checks successful, no migration.

Exact-head CI run `44917973935`, successful rust-test job `136887571562`, upload-log-selected JUnit artifact `14713000796`: 2,813 cases, no failures. All fourteen picture tests and the new assign/view regression are present and passed.

Independent local baseline adds one focused same-seat/dead/closed/mixed-holder/kept-seat control to the frozen source in an owned archive, then runs `just shared-build -- test -p pij-daemon --lib picture -- --nocapture --then test -p pij-daemon --test directory_http per_pr_instances_ -- --nocapture`: exit 0, fifteen picture tests and the assign/view regression passed. No product worktree was edited.

Author mutation patches/log summaries were inspected at the explicitly supplied `/tmp/f272/` paths. Each independent M1/M2 grouping mutant failed the new library and HTTP regression; M3 warning-scope mutant failed the HTTP regression. Those receipts were made before rustfmt/main convergence.

Independent requested-head grouping mutant (`find(|_| true)`, retaining the distinct-seat guard): `just shared-build -- test -p pij-daemon --lib -- per_pr_instances reviewer_323 --nocapture`: exit 101, both tests failed on the intended assertions, including the bare-plus-instance case. Independent warning mutant (ignore instance equality): `just shared-build -- test -p pij-daemon --test directory_http per_pr_instances_ -- --nocapture`: exit 101, the no-warning assertion failed for a different seat assigned to a different instance. Both compiled successfully. Each mutant was applied alone.

Both production guards are restored; `directory.rs` matches the frozen source byte-for-byte, and `picture.rs` differs only by the retained reviewer test patch. The baseline command returned exit 0 again: fifteen picture tests and one assign/view regression passed.

Local boot is dependency-limited under C25; exact-head CI is the broad test proof. All local cargo runs use the resolved shared target, shared-build lock, niceness 19, and four jobs.

`harness checks --quick --json`: exit 1, missing worktree dependencies and incompatible ambient Biome; native Copilot contracts, SDK, and skill checks passed. No local full-gate success is claimed and no shared dependencies were linked or installed.

Evidence retained: `pr323-reviewer-control.patch`, the grouping/warning mutation patches and logs, baseline/restored logs, local-checks envelope and exact-head JUnit archive. The owned temporary source archive is removed; the product worktree remains unchanged.

**Harness lesson:** retain the same-seat duplicate-row/kept-seat oracle beside the new instance tests; identities are seats, not assignment-row addresses.
